sentences.text: Macroplata is an extinct genus containing a single basal rhomaleosaurid plesiosaurid species.
This animal possessed a neck twice as long as its skull, a feature unlike that of pliosaurs.
Scientists estimate its body length was between 4.38 and 4.65 meters, with a mass of approximately 604 kilograms.
The type species Macroplata tenuiceps is known from a nearly complete skeleton found in the Blue Lias Formation of Harbury, Warwickshire, UK.
The holotype and only known specimen is a nearly complete skeleton named BMNH R5488, discovered in Warwickshire, England.
Macroplata likely fed on fish using its sharp, needle-like teeth.
Large shoulder bones suggest Macroplata used powerful forward strokes to swim fast.
The better-preserved maxilla of the holotype has 18 tooth sockets, with the smallest located at the back.
Macroplata belongs to the family Rhomaleosauridae.
Macroplata is classified within the suborder Pliosauroidea.
The species Macroplata longirostris was reclassified in 2011 as a pliosaurid in the genus Hauffiosaurus.
Macroplata lived in the Early Jurassic in the UK and grew up to 5 meters long.
There is a debate regarding the size of the pineal foramen in Macroplata, with sources claiming it was both large and small.
